info.title: CF Meet internal service HTTP conventions
info.description:
Transport conventions every CF Meet internal (service-to-service) HTTP API uses. Internal routes live under /internal/v1/ and require service authentication by construction. Network location (localhost, same VM, cluster, VPC or Docker network) never authenticates a caller.

Every internal request carries exactly one of each header: X-CF-Service-Authorization (`Bearer <service token>`, see cfmeet.platform.service-token-header and cfmeet.platform.service-token-claims), X-CF-Request-Id (new for every hop) and X-CF-Correlation-Id (stable across the causal operation). Both id headers must equal the request_id / correlation_id claims signed in the token. Internal requests never carry a customer `Authorization` credential; customer routes never accept a service token.

This document defines components only. Concrete internal operations are registered by the service that owns them when they are implemented.

cfServiceAuth.name: X-CF-Service-Authorization
cfServiceAuth.description: `Bearer <token>`: JWS compact serialization, alg EdDSA (Ed25519), typ cf-service+jwt, signed by the calling service's own key for exactly one audience and runtime environment; lifetime at most 300 seconds. Permissions come only from the receiver's trust bundle.

CfRequestId.name: X-CF-Request-Id
CfRequestId.description: Identifier of this hop. Must equal the signed request_id claim.

CfCorrelationId.name: X-CF-Correlation-Id
CfCorrelationId.description: Identifier of the causal operation. Must equal the signed correlation_id claim.

InternalErrorEnvelope.description: Normalized internal authentication / authorization failure. It never says why authentication failed (unknown issuer, bad signature, wrong audience, ...); the reason is operator telemetry only.

InternalAuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, unverifiable or unacceptable service token, or id headers that disagree with the signed claims.

InternalPermissionDenied.description: The authenticated service is not granted the permission this operation requires by the receiver's trust policy.
